title: Take a used commode pail out from under its seat: draw it forward off its brackets, keep it level, set it down
instruction: Take the used pail out from under the commode seat and set it down on the floor in front of the commode without spilling it.
context: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131.00; 1,448,910 US jobs, BLS May 2025) have the Core task 'Supply, collect, or empty bedpans.', which at least 67% of them rate relevant (about 0.97 million); a nursing-assistant checklist for the bedside commode begins 'Remove the receptacle from the commode and cover it.' Drive's 11135-1 manual says 'Slide pail in from front of commode': the pail hangs by its rim on two brackets under the seat, so it comes out drawn forward between the front legs, then goes down on a pad on the floor to be covered (a bedpan-washer maker's guide names 'the floor with an underlay'). Its plastic bail pivots at the pail's ends; under the seat the frame's front tube keeps it from standing up until the pail is 0.18 m out, though its centre leaves the brackets' ends at 0.12 m; in that span the bail, held level, carries the 1.3 kg 15 cm from the grip (about 1.9 N m), so the pail pitches forward unless its front is held up. Tipped or set down hard, it splashes waste.
setup: Metres; x forward, y to the robot's left, z up; origin midway between the arm bases (0, +/-0.305); the bench top (z = 0.7475) stands for the floor. At true size: Drive's 11135-1 drop-arm commode (Drive: 26.25 in outside, 25.75 in between arms, 26 in between legs, seat 23.25 x 18.5 in, seat 17.5 to 22 in high; listings: 21 in deep, 33 in high) and its 12 qt pail. (1) The commode, fixed, shaped as in its manual's figure 1, its front (the pail's way out, as the manual has it) toward the robot, centred at (0.70, 0): a frame of 25 mm grey steel tube, four legs with rubber tips at the corners of its 0.667 wide x 0.533 deep footprint (leg centres 0.642 apart across, 0.617 clear between the front legs), the seat frame's tubes 0.40 to 0.425 up (its front tube over the pail's way out), diagonal side braces, low side and back ties; both drop arms up, foam pads 0.654 apart; the back legs run up into a loop to 0.838 with a half-moon back pad; the moulded grey seat 0.591 x 0.470 with its round opening, top 0.445 above the floor (its lowest), its lid closed. Two flat steel pail brackets under the seat along x, 0.314 apart centres, 20 mm wide, 10 mm thick, tops 0.375 up, hung from the side tubes, open at their front ends (x = 0.47), 5 mm behind the seat's front edge (bracket and seat thickness estimates). (2) The pail, free, white plastic, one rigid body, tapered with round corners: rim flange 0.348 across y by 0.25 along x, 10 mm thick, its top 0.385 up, resting on both brackets under the seat, its front flush with the seat's front edge; body 0.288 x 0.189 at the rim, 0.24 x 0.15 at the bottom, 0.19 deep (from a 13.7 x 9.8 x 8.5 in listing; shape an estimate); its handle Drive's 11108 bail as in its photos: a moulded plastic band 14 x 6 mm with a ridged grip 16 mm round and 120 mm long at its middle, 0.37 across between its ends and 0.15 from its pivots to the grip, on a free hinge through two lugs on the pail's end walls 40 mm under the rim (below the brackets), colliding; at rest it lies folded forward against the pail's front, its grip 0.23 up (sizes estimates scaled from the listed length). Empty 0.5 kg plus 0.8 kg of contents (1.3 kg; estimates); centred at (0.59, 0). Friction on the pail 0.6 static, 0.5 dynamic (estimates). Its cover lies off, on the floor beside the commode's right side (0.70, -0.52). (3) The floor in front of the commode, x below 0.43, clear. Nothing else is on the bench. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. The right hand goes in under the folded bail's grip, 58 cm from its base, jaws 40 mm apart, swings the bail up level under the front tube (it cannot stand up there), pinches the grip and draws the pail 90 mm forward. The left hand pinches the rim's front strip left of the bail, 44 cm from its base. Both draw it on 0.31 m, level, off the brackets between the front legs (its centre passes the brackets' ends on the way, the left holding the front up), carry it level and set it down in front of the commode, and let go (payload 1.5 kg an arm, grip about 40 N a finger). The README lists every collider. Real trial: a Drive 11135-1 on the bench, clamped or sandbagged so it cannot slide when the pail binds; 0.8 L of water, never real waste; the pail's bail free on its pivots, as sold; a disposable underpad on a towel where the pail is set down; silicone sleeves on the gripper pads.
scoring: Judged on the pail as it ends; only failures latch. Real trial: 0.8 L of water in the pail, an underpad on a towel where it is set down, a phone filming the side at 240 fps beside a printed millimetre scale and protractor (pitch), and a second phone facing the commode's front for roll (kit about $175, README). Terms. MOVED: the pail more than 5 mm from its start. SPLASH: once moved, its axis tilted over 15 degrees (spillage; estimate: a margin for slosh as the weight arrives, well inside the about 49 degrees at which 0.8 L lying 17 mm deep would reach the rim at rest; real trial: water on the pad or floor in a photo of the floor and the pail, or a pitch or roll over 15 degrees on either video against its protractor). HARD: once moved, a hard landing: each bottom corner is read the first step it is under 2 mm from the floor, and any corner moving down faster than 0.3 m/s then voids the run (estimate; the demo touches down at 0.06 m/s; speed higher up does not count, so a pail lowered fast and slowed before it lands is not HARD; real trial: the same speed on the 240 fps side video, the lowest bottom corner taking fewer than 4 frames, 17 ms, to cross its last 5 mm before contact, which is over 0.3 m/s; a knock you can hear or a bounce is only a prompt to measure). DRAWN: drawn 50 mm or more toward the robot (real trial: a tape mark on a bracket 50 mm in front of the flange's start). OUT: the whole flange in front of the brackets' open ends (real trial: the gap on the video). DOWN: the bottom within 5 mm of the floor, the flange wholly in front of a line 40 mm in front of the brackets' ends, within 10 degrees of level, every part of both hands 30 mm or more from the whole pail (rim, walls, bottom) and its bail, and still, for the last 1 s (real trial: resting on the pad, in front of a tape line on the bench; a phone level app on the rim; the scale on the video for the 30 mm and the stillness). DROPPED: off the brackets, no part of a hand within 25 mm, more than 20 mm up and falling (real trial: the video). TIPPED: axis over 70 degrees. Tiers: 1.0 DOWN with no SPLASH; 0.5 OUT, not down, no SPLASH; 0.4 DOWN after a SPLASH; 0.25 DRAWN only, or OUT after a SPLASH; else 0. Zeros that stick: HARD, DROPPED, TIPPED. A SPLASH sticks as a cap: no 1.0 or 0.5 after it. DRAWN, OUT and DOWN count only while true, so a pail set down and lifted back over the brackets' ends scores 0.25 (lifted but still out of the brackets: 0.5). Dragging it along the floor has no rule of its own; a drag that tilts it over 15 degrees is a SPLASH (0.4 at best). Costs nothing by itself: which hand draws and which supports; where the pail is gripped; how fast it is drawn; any tilt under 15 degrees; where past the line it is set down. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.4, 0.5, 1.0.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo reaches 1.0 at step 699 (34.95 s).
reset_notes: Nothing is random. Empty the pail and refill it with 0.8 L of water; replace the underpad if wet and dry the towel; slide the pail onto the brackets to its tape mark, the flange square on both; check the commode's clamps; both arms at their ready pose. About 2 minutes.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Contents are part of the pail's 1.3 kg (real: 0.8 L of liquid); a spill is read from tilt over 15 deg, a hard landing from a corner's speed over 0.3 m/s at first floor contact (real trial: under 4 frames of 240 fps over the last 5 mm; estimates). The bail is a free 50 g hinge on its lugs. Drive 11135-1 at published sizes; the rest estimates. Hand-clear reads a point lattice over each whole gripper, wrist to fingertips; palm contact is unreachable, so checked by geometry only.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0. Demo: 1.0 (both hands, 699 steps, 34.95 s, GPU). One hand by bail or rim 0; drawn 100 mm only 0.25; set down, dragged 10 cm 0.4; one hand lets go 0.5; let go 12 cm, 15 or 19 mm up, or tipped 60 mm 0; tipped 5 mm, or lowered fast and slowed, 1.0; nothing 0.
